issues.problem: LPIPS convention differs from the official test.py. Official lpipsPyTorch (3DGS copy) feeds the [0,1] gamma image straight into AlexNet + the LPIPS ScalingLayer (mean [-.030,-.088,-.188], std [.458,.448,.450]), i.e. NO [0,1]->[-1,1] rescale. The plugin feeds t*2-1 into the lpips package, the standard convention, so it is not the one behind the paper's 0.086.
issues.evidence: source/code/test.py evaluate(): lpips(image, gt_image, net_type='alex') on [0,1] tensors; lpipsPyTorch/modules/networks.py BaseNet.z_score applied to raw input. Measured on evidence/smoke-1 (ball, 4 aligned test views): lpips-alex with [-1,1] = 0.470 (what test_tpo.json reports), with [0,1] (official) = 0.388, about 17% lower.
issues.fix: Add lpips_alex_official = lpips.LPIPS(net='alex')(x01, y01) with x01 the UNclamped gamma image in [0,1] NCHW (same weights as lpipsPyTorch), and make it the headline LPIPS. Keep the [-1,1] value as a secondary column.

issues.problem: Official PSNR on an unbatched [3,H,W] tensor: utils/image_utils.psnr does view(3,-1), giving a per-channel PSNR, and then .mean(). The image is not clamped. The plugin uses the global-MSE PSNR on the clamped image.
issues.evidence: smoke-1: global clamped 22.510 vs official per-channel unclamped 22.528 (+0.02 dB)
issues.fix: Report psnr_official = mean_c(-10 log10 mse_c) on the unclamped tone-mapped render.

issues.problem: SSIM and LPIPS are computed on after.clamp(0,1). Official evaluate() does not clamp; only the pose loss clamps.
issues.evidence: test.py evaluate: image = scene.tone_mapping(render(...)) with no clamp
issues.fix: Compute the official-convention metrics on the unclamped image. The effect is negligible but trivial to fix.

issues.problem: Hybrid schedule for nu: the paper's lr (3e-3) with the code's schedule (0 until 30k, then exponential decay to 1e-7 at 150k; frozen at 100k by curve_end_iter). The paper says all motion lrs halve every 15k. Under this schedule nu is learned only in steps 30k-100k.
issues.evidence: paper experiments.tex l.58; train.py alignment_func; motion.alternate_optimization at curve_end_iter
issues.fix: Keep it (it is the code's schedule and the comment '# 3e-3' sits on it). Label it in the report as code-schedule + paper-lr.

issues.problem: The Inria rasterizer caps per-Gaussian alpha at 0.99 in the forward pass. gsplat caps at 0.999. The straight-through opacity cap at 0.999 restores gradients but does not reproduce the 0.99 forward cap.
issues.fix: Document it as a fidelity gap (small effect).

issues.problem: The release also ships images_4/*.png at 600x400 (Deblur-NeRF's own downsample, used by the Deblur-NeRF/ExBluRF rows). The plugin instead uses a PIL /4 of the full-res JPGs. This is the most likely official path, because COLMAP names are .png, images/ holds .jpg, and readColmapCameras has an explicit .jpg fallback; but the README's '--resolution $RESOLUTION' is unspecified.
issues.fix: Keep PIL /4 as the headline. Optionally note the images_4 alternative in the report.

issues.problem: The paper's 3DGS row (21.69) is post-optimised vanilla 3DGS. Our gsplat ss-eval baseline is unaligned and has no gamma, so the improvement comparison is not like-for-like.
issues.fix: If a baseline delta is wanted, run the same post-optimisation (without gamma) on the gsplat checkpoint. Otherwise compare absolute numbers only and say so.

losses.py:create_rgb uses L1(blur_lin, gt^2.2) = official code form; the paper applies gamma to the render (documented)
losses.py:smoothness, mean-L1 per code; the paper writes an L2 sum (documented)

probe_assessment.why: independent de Casteljau and matrix_exp references; init must reproduce the COLMAP pose
compares against independent per-pose gsplat renders and checks the blur differs from sharp; checks freezing before 1000 and at/after 100k
nu must get a gradient and move after 30k (nu0 variant: must not move)
numpy reference GT^2.2 and render^(1/2.2); fails if the tone curve is dropped
independent numpy formula and schedule end points; hinge reference
a grad of 3e-4 must not densify at 600 but must at 25000; reset and prune semantics; extent formula
a perturbed pose must be recovered (PSNR rises), which a no-op cannot do; it does not check the metric conventions, hence the LPIPS issue

fidelity_gaps_confirmed: Verified against official arguments/__init__.py + train.py: 150k steps, N=21, order 9, SH 2, Clamp opacity + hinge 0.1 on the raw value, no D-SSIM, theta 4e-4->2e-4 expon over 25k, densify from 500 / every 200 / until 75k, reset every 3000 (while <75k) to min(o,0.1), opacity-only prune, percent_dense 0.01, xyz lr 1.6e-4->1.6e-6 x the DeblurGS extent (min(p10 cam-to-pcd-mean, 1.1 max cam spread)) with no delay, curve lr 1e-2/1e-3 x 0.5^((s-999)/15000), curve trainable [1000,100000), single sub-frame at t=0 before 1000, lambda_t 1e-3->1e-5, random background per step, linear-space L1 vs GT^2.2.

nu lr: the code default is 0.0 with the comment '# 3e-3'. The only commit (e0587475) is titled 'update lambda_t_smooth/temporarily disabled alignment'. Table 2 shows learned nu helps. So the Table 1 runs almost certainly used nu learning (3e-3), and possibly the older (paper) lambda_smooth values.

Data: the official loader sorts by name, splits int(name) % hold == 0 using the hold=N file, and falls back from the COLMAP .png name to images/*.jpg. With -r 4 it does a PIL default-resample resize to 600x400. The plugin matches (ball: 23 train / 4 test, 600x400, f=421.1).

Runtime: views sampled with replacement (official: shuffled stack); the Gaussian Adam step runs before densify/reset (official: a densified or reset step skips the Gaussian update); SH degree rises at step 1001, not 1000; alpha cap 0.999 vs 0.99.
Post-opt uses only the test images and test poses; the scene params are detached. This matches test.py and paper Sec. 4.2.

No per-scene numbers exist for Real Motion Blur (no supplementary in the e-print; README has no tables). The only per-scene numbers are Table 2, on unreleased ExBlur-NP. A commented-out row in ablation_table.tex (26.16/0.871/0.072) is an earlier variant, not a target.
summary: The port is faithful to the official training code line by line: trajectory, nu, gamma-in-loss, smoothness, hinge, annealed densification, schedules, extent and test-pose optimisation all check out, and 10 pytest tests pass. One major issue: the evaluator's LPIPS uses the [-1,1] input convention, while official test.py feeds [0,1] images into lpipsPyTorch. On the smoke run this changes LPIPS-Alex from 0.470 to 0.388, so the 0.086 target is not comparable until fixed. PSNR (per-channel mean, unclamped) and SSIM clamping are minor. Headline method: deblurgs (nu lr 3e-3); deblurgs-nu0 is an optional 2-scene bracket. There is no cheaper faithful target: all 10 scenes at 150k steps are required.
